lexical.anchor: [S] 13.3 identifies Kṛṣṇa as the knower in all fields — a universal knower. DERIVED — KnowledgeOS has, at 31.19, an information-theoretic impossibility theorem: 'No algorithm can recover information that the observation function destroys.' A universal knower is exactly what that theorem forbids. So the source's second knower-level has no KnowledgeOS image, and the reason is mathematical. This is the lens working correctly. It offered a structure; the mathematics refused half of it; the refusal is more informative than an accepted analogy would have been. RX for the universal level, R5 for the individual one.

notations: 31.19: "No algorithm can recover information that the observation function destroys."

# universal-knower-refuted-by-observation-destruction-impossibility

**Scope(s):** OBJECT · **Row count:** 8 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** DORMANT · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** `31.19: "No algorithm can recover information that the observation function destroys."`, `RX universal knower, R5 individual knower` · **Aliases:** `universal knower refutation`
**Candidate group membership (NOT an identity claim):**
Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.

## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)
- **OBJECT-INDEX** batch `B0050`, scope `OBJECT`: The Gita sub-series' one genuine falsification result: Gita 13.3 textually attests Krishna as 'the knower in all fields' (a universal knower). KnowledgeOS corpus location 31.19 states an information-theoretic impossibility theorem: 'No algorithm can recover information that the observation function destroys.' A universal knower (one who could know a field regardless of what any observation function destroys) is exactly what this theorem forbids. Verdict: RX (rejected) for the universal-knower level, R5 (formally supported) for the individual-knower (kshetra-jna) level -- the source's own richer claim is refuted by independently-derived KnowledgeOS mathematics, judged more informative than an accepted analogy would have been.
